call_points.text: Oil Seed utilisation seen at around 80% this year, up from 65-70% now.
Animal Health to grow in double digits in FY27.
Oil Seed performance expected equivalent or better than Q4 up to September; crop call after October.
Broiler chick and contract farming volumes targeted 2-5% higher than last year.
No further Oil Seed capex for a year; all 3 units to be made resilient first.
Working capital availability of about ₹160 Cr; no plan to add term or working capital debt.
CCI notice received on parent breeding-farm practices; Venky's says the listed entity is not affected as of now.

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (standalone): revenue ₹1,100.47 Cr, net profit ₹96.72 Cr (includes ₹4.65 Cr from discontinued operations; continuing operations ₹101.37 Cr).
Venky's (India) Limited’s Board, chaired by Rohan Ajay Bhagwat, recommended a final dividend of ₹10 per equity share (100%) for FY2026, pending shareholder approval.
Venky’s (India) Limited held an investor conference call on 15 May 2026 discussing FY2026 results, with audio recording available via link.
Venky's held its Q4FY26 earnings call on 15 May 2026, guiding Oil Seed utilisation to about 80% for FY27 and Animal Health margins at 22-23% and above.
Venkateshwara Hatcheries Private Limited, acting as promoters and persons in concert with Venky's (India) Limited, declared no encumbrance on their held equity shares on April 3, 2026.

watchlist.text: Shareholder approval for dividend at the ensuing Annual General Meeting

watchlist.response: CFO said the company would get back on the question; no figure given.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for the SPF egg segment's margin and outlook.

watchlist.response: Management declined to quantify, saying it cannot comment as of now but is optimistic on double-digit growth.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked how much revenue the new Animal Health plant can add.

watchlist.response: Management called the combined portfolio complementary and said it had taken the suggestion, without committing to any action.
watchlist.text: Analysts repeatedly asked about splitting off and separately listing Animal Health.
